---

### CLI wire-trace flag contract (Proposed; acceptance open)

Status: Proposed. Resolves open point 1 for the CLI default tier only; server tiered profiles stay open. Claims no implementation, no Verified status, weakens no normative control; on conflict the normative text wins.

1. Surface: `bitty-devtools trace start --wire-trace [--duration-ms <n>] [--max-bytes <n>] [--include-input] [connection options] [--json]`, `trace stop --wire-trace --trace-id <id>`, `trace fetch-chunk --wire-trace --trace-id <id> --offset <n>`. `--wire-trace` is argv-presence-only, default off; without it every `trace` verb is a usage error (exit 2). `inspect` never accepts `--wire-trace` or any `--trace-*` flag. There is no environment, configuration, build-flag, `BITTY_CTL_ELEVATE`, or automation-bearer path to enable it.
2. Scope: trace verbs use the live socket path only and require `debug.trace` (server-enforced per call via `isValidMethodForScope`); `debug.inspect` alone fails closed with `ScopeDenied`. The flag never widens `inspect` and never requests `debug.control`.
3. Defaults and bounds (UTF-8 bytes): duration default 10000 ms, range 1..300000; maxBytes default 524288, range 1..4194304; chunk fixed 262144 with scalar-boundary split, byte-accurate offset, and continuation flag; retention/filter/drop-policy/coalesce are server defaults (5 min / 4 MiB / 4 traces, DropOldest, budget-coalesce) and not argv-tunable in v1.
4. Privacy: input markers default off (`--include-input` opts in); typed redaction (P0-AC-026) before queue; spool files mode `0600`; export preview equals actual export byte-for-byte; every response is untrusted observation data.
5. Limits: RC-9 rate/frame/connection shedding, 32-record/8 KiB batching, 8 KiB per-record cap, and AbortSignal cancellation apply unchanged.
   Open point 1 resolves to the CLI tier above; tiered server profiles remain open under item 1. Verification extends verify-8 (redaction/0600/preview-equals-export over CLI chunks) and verify-10 (no-bypass audit of the full `--wire-trace`/`--trace-*` surface) with the negative-test list in the acceptance record.

---

4. Negative-test list (all must fail closed, zero partial state)
   N1 trace start/stop/fetch-chunk without --wire-trace => exit 2. N2 inspect + --wire-trace/--trace-* => exit 2. N3 --wire-trace=false/0/value => exit 2 (presence only). N4 --plugin-style flag-as-value for --duration-ms/--max-bytes/--trace-id/--offset => exit 2. N5 inspect scope calls startTrace/stopTrace/fetchTraceChunk => ScopeDenied exit 7. N6 duration 0/negative/float/abc/>300000 => exit 2. N7 maxBytes 0/>4194304 => exit 2. N8 offset negative/>byteCount/non-integer => typed error, exit per exitCodeForError. N9 default (no --include-input) seeded input/clipboard/env absent; with --include-input redaction still applies. N10 seeded secret in chunk/preview absent; 0600 asserted; tampered export => PreviewMismatch. N11 multi-byte UTF-8 split stays scalar-boundary; counts use UTF-8 bytes not .length. N12 BITTY_WIRE_TRACE=1/config/BITTY_CTL_ELEVATE/automation bearer do not enable trace. N13 trace verb with no socket/headless mock => exit 6, no rows. N14 RC-9 overrun/oversized frame/>16 conns shed with budget/transport errors + counted drops. N15 missing --trace-id/unknown verb/unknown flag => exit 2 with USAGE.
5. Non-goals: no tiered profiles, no filter/retention argv, no tunable chunk, no pixels/raw-PTY channel, no MCP streaming, no control escalation, no persistence of bearer/trace grant.

PROPOSAL PART 1/2 — EXACT RFC AMENDMENT PROSE (paste-ready, Proposed Amendment A4; claims no implementation/acceptance): --- BEGIN PROSE --- ### CLI watch mode — inspect-only polling (Proposed, Amendment A4, acceptance open) > Status: Proposed (CTX-0067, issue #121 child of #72). This section proposes an inspect-only watch contract for bitty-devtools inspect --watch. It claims no implementation, no acceptance, no compatibility promise, and no Verified status. It adds no protocol method, scope, transport, queue family, or budget; it reuses only accepted v1 debug.inspect methods (bitty.debug/listPlugins, listSubscriptions, getBudgets), framing (1 MiB inbound, 256 KiB chunks, RC-10), per-wakeup batching (32 records or 8 KiB), per-consumer queue bounds, RC-9 rate limits, and the sampling-only profiling posture. Where it conflicts with a normative control, the normative text wins. 1. Surface (no new methods): bitty-devtools inspect (--plugins|--subscriptions --plugin <id>|--budgets --plugin <id>) [--generation <n>] [--json] [--watch] [--interval-ms <n>] [--max-ticks <n>] plus existing --socket/--instance. --watch without an inspect selector, with unknown flags, with --generation <1, --interval-ms/--max-ticks out of range, or with an option value beginning with - is a usage error (exit 2). Without --watch behavior is unchanged single-shot. 2. Inspect-only, denial asserted: every tick dispatches exactly one accepted inspect method over the already-connected IpcTransport via the existing dispatch/dispatchLive path and renders via the existing table/JSON path. The watch loop grants and pins debug.inspect only; it never grants, asserts, or inherits debug.trace or debug.control, never calls streamEvents/startTrace/stopTrace, control suspend/resume/dispose, synthesizeInput/captureFrame/frameHash, or any automation bearer path. A server ScopeDenied/trace/control demand fails closed (exit 7) and terminates the loop with zero further ticks; a missing inspect grant is a client ScopeDenied before any byte is sent. Connection alone grants nothing. 3. Interval floor, jitter, RC-9: --interval-ms default 2000, floor WATCH_FLOOR_MS 1000, ceiling 60000; values outside fail closed (exit 2). Effective sleep per tick is interval_ms * (1 + U) with U uniform in [-0.10, +0.10] drawn per tick from a non-crypto PRNG (jitter is anti-thundering-herd only, never a security boundary). Floor rationale: 1000ms is 10x the accepted sampling floor 100ms (CTX-0189) so watch polling cannot become per-frame tracing and preserves PB-4/PB-7 neutrality; steady state is ~0.5-1 req/s, two orders below RC-9 sustained 100 req/s / 200 burst, so a lone watcher never approaches shedding. Every tick still passes IpcTransport RateLimiter.check + peer re-verification; a RateLimited/TransportFull verdict surfaces as typed budget error (exit 6), skips emission for that tick, and defers to the next scheduled tick — never a tight retry loop. --- END PART 1 (continues in PART 2) ---
